result: At exact rmcp-v3.1.4 release source, TaskManager stores task state in Arc<Mutex<TaskManagerInner>> with a HashMap keyed by task_id. get_task, update_task, and cancel_task each lock that mutex, opportunistically sweep TTL state, then address the current entry only by task_id. update_task accepts only inputResponses, removes a matching currently-pending key and ignores unknown/already-answered/superseded keys; TaskContext separately enforces input-request key uniqueness for the lifetime of the task. cancel_task sets cancel_requested=true and signals the current operation, with no expected-old state. No generation, version, expected status/value, CAS precondition, monotonic attempt fence, or historical write fence is checked by these three operations. Therefore the stock manager provides current-process serialization and per-input-key replay narrowing, but not a task-wide generation/CAS/history fence. This finding is scoped only to this exact release source and these TaskManager entry points; it does not claim absence of an application-level fence outside TaskManager.
